current: Both formal u-pw and the developing u-pl raw flexible-confinement path use the uncorrected kernel gradient. Stress-rate gradient correction and symmetric Darcy correction do not correct external traction.
position: During bounded Cryer integration/accuracy review and before the next formal long-run/server admission. Coordinate with the literal Lian Eq23 operator comparison; preserve all existing formal data.
audit_order: Reproduce the actual source-clock ramp, quadrature, current density/J volumes, kernel support and native curved-surface geometry; do not change time alignment or q0 to fit the peak.

Check raw internal total stress plus raw confinement pointwise for uniform compression. In the u-pl branch a_load=(2q/rho_i)*sum(Vj*gradWij), so uniform total stress=-qI cancels it term by term with the same quadrature. Test both actual CPU/GPU arithmetic and source-telemetry gating.

If testing a correction, first compare raw/raw with a mathematically matched stress/load pair. Do not correct the load alone. Check constant-stress cancellation, linear-field consistency, pair/global force and torque behavior, conditioning and curved-neighborhood errors.

Uniform spherical pressure has near-zero net vector force by symmetry; that alone cannot establish correct loading magnitude or transmission. Also inspect radial work/virial against geometric volume, inward traction measures, radial total-stress profiles and the fixed material center response.

Only a low-cost, supported candidate proceeds to native startup/ramp-hold-drain/half/backend gates and pressure-peak amplitude/time plus radial-field/theory comparisons. Operator-option changes are not half-step errors; no automatic physical acceptance or unlimited tuning.
comparison_limits: u-pl J-derived inertia/quadrature/complete Darcy and stabilization differ together from retained u-pw. Do not call a whole-framework comparison an isolated correction test. Preserve finite-Kw/finite-radius theory, fixed18 native center IDs, drainage-relative tau, actual saved times and full startup.
